# Method for Producing Metal-Plastic Composite Webs or Sheets

## Overview of the Invention

The present invention relates to a method for producing composite webs or sheets characterized by a sandwich-type construction, comprising a lower metal cover layer, an upper metal cover layer, and a plastic core layer that is integrally bonded between the two metal layers. This composite structure combines the mechanical strength and durability of metal with the lightweight properties and versatility of plastic, resulting in a material suitable for a wide range of industrial applications.

## Basic Process Principle

At the core of the invention lies a process in which a first metal strip, a second metal strip, and a plastic web are brought together in a coordinated manner and subsequently bonded to one another through the application of pressure, heat, or a combination of both. Through this bonding step, the three individual layers—the two metal strips and the intermediate plastic web—are permanently joined together to form a unified, integral composite structure.

## Two-Stage Process Architecture

A distinguishing feature of the invention is the division of the overall manufacturing process into two separate, distinct process stages:

### Stage One: Pretreatment Line

In the first stage, both metal strips are individually and continuously coated with an adhesion promoter. This pretreatment step is carried out in a dedicated pretreatment line, which operates independently of the subsequent laminating process. The purpose of this adhesion promoter coating is to enhance the bonding capability of the metal surfaces, thereby ensuring a strong and durable connection to the plastic core layer in the later bonding step.

Following the coating process, the treated metal strips are wound into coils. This winding step allows the coated strips to be stored temporarily or transported to another location, effectively decoupling the pretreatment stage from the subsequent lamination stage in terms of both timing and location.

### Stage Two: Laminating Line

In the second stage, the coated and previously wound metal strips are unwound again and brought together with the plastic web in a separate laminating line, which is spatially and operationally distinct from the pretreatment line. Within this laminating line, the two metal strips and the plastic core layer are continuously combined and bonded together through the ongoing application of pressure and heat.

This continuous bonding process results in the metal strips and the plastic web being integrally joined into a finished composite web or sheet, thereby completing the manufacturing process.

## Advantages of the Two-Stage Approach

By separating the adhesion-promoter coating process from the actual lamination process, and by conducting these two steps in distinct process lines, the invention offers several practical benefits:

- **Process flexibility**: The pretreatment and lamination stages can be carried out independently, potentially at different times or locations, allowing for more flexible production planning.
- **Efficient use of coated material**: Since the coated metal strips are wound into coils after pretreatment, they can be produced in advance and stored until needed for the lamination process, thus decoupling production capacities of the two stages.
- **Optimized process control**: Each stage can be optimized separately with respect to its own specific process parameters, such as coating thickness and curing conditions in the pretreatment line, or pressure and temperature profiles in the laminating line.

This two-stage architecture, combining an independent pretreatment line with a separate continuous laminating line, thus represents a significant aspect of the invention, enabling an efficient and controllable process for manufacturing high-quality metal-plastic composite webs or sheets.

# Method for Producing Composite Webs or Sheets with Metal Cover Layers and Plastic Core Layer

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a method for producing composite webs or sheets comprising metal cover layers bonded to opposite sides of a plastic core layer. Such composite materials find widespread application in industries requiring lightweight yet durable panel materials, including automotive manufacturing, construction, appliance housing production, and architectural cladding systems.

## Background

Traditional methods for manufacturing metal-plastic-metal composite materials typically involve an integrated, single-line process wherein metal strips are treated with adhesion-promoting substances and immediately thereafter laminated to a plastic core material in a continuous, uninterrupted sequence of operations. While functional, this conventional approach presents significant limitations in terms of production flexibility, line utilization efficiency, and the ability to optimize each processing stage independently. Any variation in metal strip specifications, adhesion promoter formulations, or laminating parameters necessitates adjustments to the entire integrated production line, resulting in downtime and reduced throughput.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention overcomes these limitations by fundamentally restructuring the production process into two distinct and separately operable process lines: a pretreatment line and a laminating line.

### Pretreatment Line

In the first stage of the inventive method, two separate metal strips—which will ultimately form the upper and lower cover layers of the finished composite—are fed through a dedicated pretreatment line. Within this line, each metal strip undergoes a continuous coating process wherein an adhesion promoter is applied uniformly across the strip surface. This adhesion promoter coating serves to enhance the bonding characteristics between the metal surface and the subsequently applied plastic core material, ensuring durable and reliable adhesion in the finished composite product.

Following the application of the adhesion promoter, each coated metal strip is wound into a coil for storage and subsequent handling. This winding step is significant, as it allows the pretreated metal strips to be produced, inspected, and stored independently of the laminating process, without requiring immediate integration into a continuous production sequence.

### Laminating Line

In a separate and distinct process stage, the pretreated and coiled metal strips are unwound and fed into a dedicated laminating line. Within this laminating line, the two coated metal strips are brought together with a plastic web material, which is positioned between them to form the core layer of the composite structure. The three components—the two metal cover layers and the intervening plastic core—are then subjected to a combination of pressure and heat within the laminating line, causing the adhesion promoter coating to activate and effect a durable bond between the metal cover layers and the plastic core layer.

### Key Innovation: Process Separation

The central and inventive aspect of this method lies in the deliberate separation of the pretreatment process from the laminating process into two distinct, independently operable production lines. This structural division, rather than being a mere logistical rearrangement, provides substantial technical and economic advantages over conventional integrated single-line approaches.

## Advantages of the Invention

The separation of pretreatment and laminating operations into distinct lines yields several notable benefits:

1. **Enhanced Production Flexibility**: Because the pretreatment line operates independently of the laminating line, metal strips can be coated with adhesion promoter and stockpiled in advance, allowing manufacturers to build inventory of pretreated material for use as needed, independent of immediate laminating demands.

2. **Improved Line Utilization**: Each line can be operated at its own optimal speed and efficiency without being constrained by the operational parameters of the other. The pretreatment line, for instance, may run at different speeds or scheduling patterns compared to the laminating line, maximizing overall equipment utilization.

3. **Greater Manufacturing Efficiency**: By decoupling the two processes, manufacturers can address bottlenecks, perform maintenance, or make adjustments to one line without necessarily halting the other, thereby improving overall production continuity and reducing costly downtime.

4. **Simplified Quality Control**: The independent nature of the two process lines allows for more focused quality control measures at each stage—inspection and verification of the adhesion promoter coating can occur immediately after pretreatment, prior to the strip being committed to the laminating process.

5. **Adaptability to Varying Production Requirements**: This method allows manufacturers to more readily adjust to varying customer specifications, material combinations, or production volumes, since pretreated coils of metal strip can be selectively matched with different plastic core materials in the laminating line as required, without necessitating reconfiguration of the entire production system.

## Conclusion

This invention represents a significant advancement in the field of composite panel manufacturing by introducing a novel two-stage production methodology. By separating the metal strip pretreatment process from the subsequent laminating process into distinct, independently operable lines, the invention enables more efficient, flexible, and economically advantageous production of metal-plastic-metal composite webs and sheets, addressing key limitations inherent in traditional integrated single-line manufacturing approaches.

# PATENT SPECIFICATION EXCERPT

## TITLE OF INVENTION
**Method and Apparatus for Manufacturing Metal-Plastic-Metal Composite Sheets Using Separate Pretreatment and Laminating Production Lines**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to a method for manufacturing metal-plastic-metal (MPM) composite sandwich sheets, and more particularly to a manufacturing process wherein metal surface pretreatment is performed on a first, dedicated production line separate and independent from a second production line on which the pretreated metal skins are subsequently laminated with a thermoplastic core layer to form the finished composite sheet.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Metal-plastic-metal composite sheets, comprising a polymeric core (typically polyethylene or polypropylene) sandwiched between two metal skins (typically aluminum), are widely used in architectural cladding, automotive body panels, and appliance housings due to their favorable strength-to-weight ratio.

[0003] Conventional manufacturing processes integrate metal surface treatment (degreasing, chemical conversion coating, chromating or chromium-free passivation, and primer application) directly in-line with the lamination process. This integration presents several disadvantages:

  (a) Line speed mismatches — pretreatment chemical reaction/drying times differ substantially from lamination bonding times, forcing one process to bottleneck the other;

  (b) Contamination risk — volatile organic compounds and chemical fumes from pretreatment baths can contaminate the lamination environment, affecting adhesive/core bonding quality;

  (c) Limited flexibility — a single integrated line cannot be reconfigured to accommodate different metal-core combinations without full line shutdown;

  (d) Maintenance downtime — servicing of either pretreatment or lamination stations requires halting the entire combined line.

[0004] There exists a need for a manufacturing method that decouples these process stages to improve throughput, quality control, and manufacturing flexibility.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0005] The present invention provides a method of manufacturing MPM composite sheets comprising two physically and operationally separated production lines:

  **(A)** a **pretreatment line**, on which raw metal coil stock is cleaned, surface-treated, coated with a bonding primer, cured, and re-coiled for storage or transport; and

  **(B)** a **laminating line**, physically separate from the pretreatment line, on which the pretreated (and optionally stored/transported) metal coils are uncoiled, combined with a thermoplastic core via continuous lamination (e.g., roll or belt lamination under heat and pressure), cooled, and cut/re-coiled into finished composite sheet.

[0006] By decoupling the two stages, each line may be operated at its own optimal speed, in its own controlled environment, and may be independently scheduled, maintained, or reconfigured, while intermediate pretreated coil stock serves as a buffer inventory between stages.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### 1. Overview of Process Architecture

[0007] Figure 1 illustrates the overall process flow, comprising:
- Pretreatment Line **(10)**
- Intermediate Storage/Buffer Station **(20)**
- Laminating Line **(30)**

### 2. Pretreatment Line (10)

[0008] Raw metal coil **(11)** (e.g., aluminum alloy, 0.1–0.5 mm gauge) is uncoiled at uncoiler station **(12)** and passed sequentially through:

  (i) **Alkaline cleaning station (13)** — removal of rolling oils and surface contaminants via spray or immersion alkaline cleaner (pH 9–12), followed by rinse;

  (ii) **Surface conversion station (14)** — application of a chromium-free conversion coating (e.g., zirconium-based or titanium-based passivation chemistry) to enhance corrosion resistance and adhesive bonding;

  (iii) **Drying oven (15)** — peak metal temperature (PMT) of 60–120°C to remove residual moisture;

  (iv) **Primer application station (16)** — roll-coating of a polymeric bonding primer (e.g., epoxy or polyurethane-based adhesion promoter) at a dry film thickness of 1–5 microns;

  (v) **Curing oven (17)** — PMT of 200–260°C for primer crosslinking;

  (vi) **Cooling station (18)**; and

  (vii) **Recoiler (19)** — the pretreated metal coil is recoiled for storage, inventory management, or transport to the laminating line.

[0009] In a preferred embodiment, line speed of the pretreatment line (10) is selected independently from that of the laminating line (30), typically in the range of 20–80 m/min, based on curing kinetics rather than lamination throughput requirements.

### 3. Intermediate Buffer / Storage (20)

[0010] The pretreated coil (19) may be:
  (a) stored on-site in an inventory buffer for a period ranging from several hours to several months; or
  (b) transported to a physically separate laminating facility.

[0011] This decoupling permits the pretreatment line to run in campaign mode (producing multiple coils of pretreated stock in advance) independent of laminating line scheduling, and allows a single pretreatment line to supply multiple laminating lines.

### 4. Laminating Line (30)

[0012] Two pretreated metal coils **(31a, 31b)** are uncoiled at dual uncoiler stations **(32a, 32b)** and fed, top and bottom, into a continuous lamination assembly comprising:

  (i) **Core feeding station (33)** — extrusion or unwinding of a thermoplastic core sheet (e.g., low-density or linear low-density polyethylene, or polypropylene), with optional co-extruded tie-layer for enhanced adhesion, core thickness ranging from 1–6 mm;

  (ii) **Preheating station (34)** — preheating of metal skins and/or core to 150–220°C via infrared or contact heating to promote adhesive activation without primer degradation;

  (iii) **Lamination press/nip station (35)** — continuous double-belt press or calender rolls applying pressure of 0.5–5 MPa at controlled temperature to bond the sandwich structure;

  (iv) **Cooling station (36)** — controlled cooling under continued pressure/tension to prevent bow/warp and residual stress;

  (v) **Edge trimming station (37)**;

  (vi) **Cutting/recoiling station (38)** — cutting to sheet length or recoiling as continuous coil product.

[0013] Because lines (10) and (30) are physically and operationally distinct, the laminating line (30) may run at a substantially higher throughput speed (e.g., 5–30 m/min limited by cooling kinetics rather than curing kinetics) than would be achievable in a fully integrated single-pass line.

---

## EXEMPLARY CLAIMS

**Claim 1.**
A method of manufacturing a metal-plastic-metal composite sheet, comprising:

(a) on a first production line, pretreating a metal coil by:
   (i) cleaning a surface of the metal coil;
   (ii) applying a conversion coating to the cleaned surface;
   (iii) applying a bonding primer over the conversion coating; and
   (iv) curing the bonding primer to form a pretreated metal coil;

(b) recoiling the pretreated metal coil;

(c) transporting or storing the pretreated metal coil independently of a subsequent lamination process; and

(d) on a second production line, physically separate from the first production line, laminating the pretreated metal coil with a second pretreated metal coil and an interposed thermoplastic core layer under heat and pressure to form the metal-plastic-metal composite sheet;

wherein the first production line and the second production line are operated at independently selected line speeds.

**Claim 2.**
The method of claim 1, wherein the conversion coating comprises a chromium-free zirconium-based or titanium-based passivation chemistry.

**Claim 3.**
The method of claim 1, wherein step (a)(iv) comprises curing at a peak metal temperature of 200°C to 260°C, and wherein the second production line performs lamination at a line speed exceeding the line speed of the first production line.

**Claim 4.**
The method of claim 1, wherein the thermoplastic core layer comprises polyethylene, polypropylene, or a fire-retardant mineral-filled thermoplastic core, and further comprising a tie-layer disposed between the core layer and at least one of the pretreated metal coils.

**Claim 5.**
The method of claim 1, further comprising storing a plurality of pretreated metal coils produced on the first production line as buffer inventory, and selectively supplying said buffer inventory to two or more physically distinct laminating lines including the second production line.

**Claim 6.**
The method of claim 1, wherein the lamination of step (d) is performed using a continuous double-belt press applying a pressure of 0.5 to 5 MPa at a temperature sufficient to activate the bonding primer without degrading the conversion coating.

---

*[Additional claims directed to apparatus embodiments, alternative pretreatment chemistries, and specific core formulations may be appended as needed.]*

# Technical Description of a Continuous Process for Bonding Metal Strips to a Plastic Core Layer

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a continuous process for manufacturing composite laminate materials, and more particularly to a continuous method for bonding two metal strips to opposing surfaces of a thermoplastic core layer utilizing an adhesion promoter application step to achieve enhanced interlaminar bond strength suitable for architectural panels, automotive components, and other structural composite applications.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Metal-plastic composite laminates, comprising a polymeric core layer sandwiched between two metallic skin layers, are widely utilized in industries requiring materials with high strength-to-weight ratios combined with formability and vibration-damping characteristics. Conventional manufacturing methods have relied upon batch processing techniques, adhesive film lamination, or thermal bonding methods that suffer from limitations including inconsistent bond quality, low throughput, and inadequate adhesion between dissimilar material interfaces.

A persistent challenge in the art has been achieving uniform, high-strength bonding between metallic substrates and thermoplastic cores without the use of discrete adhesive films, which introduce additional processing steps, increase material costs, and may compromise the mechanical properties of the finished laminate. There exists a need in the art for a continuous, high-throughput process capable of producing metal-plastic-metal composite laminates with consistent adhesion properties suitable for demanding structural applications.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention provides a continuous process for producing a metal-plastic-metal composite laminate comprising the steps of: (a) unwinding first and second metal strips from respective supply reels; (b) surface treating at least one surface of each metal strip; (c) applying an adhesion promoter coating to the treated surface of each metal strip; (d) curing or partially curing the adhesion promoter coating; (e) extruding or feeding a thermoplastic core layer between the coated metal strips; (f) laminating the assembly under heat and pressure to form a unified composite structure; (g) cooling the composite laminate; and (h) coiling or cutting the finished laminate to desired dimensions.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

### General Process Overview

Referring to the process flow of the invention, the continuous lamination system comprises a series of sequentially arranged processing stations through which the metal strips and plastic core layer are conveyed at a controlled line speed, typically ranging from approximately 5 to 100 meters per minute, depending upon the thickness of the constituent materials and the desired residence time within each processing zone.

### Metal Strip Supply and Unwinding

In accordance with one embodiment of the invention, a first metal strip and a second metal strip are continuously unwound from respective uncoiling stations, each equipped with tension control mechanisms to maintain uniform strip tension throughout the process. The metal strips may comprise aluminum, steel, stainless steel, copper, or alloys thereof, having a thickness typically ranging from about 0.1 mm to about 1.0 mm. Each metal strip is guided through a series of tensioning rollers and accumulator systems to permit continuous operation during coil changeovers without interruption of the downstream lamination process.

### Surface Preparation

Prior to application of the adhesion promoter, the metal strips are subjected to a surface preparation step comprising one or more of the following treatments: alkaline cleaning to remove surface oils and contaminants, mechanical abrasion or brushing to increase surface roughness, chemical etching, plasma treatment, corona discharge treatment, or conversion coating (such as chromate or non-chromate conversion coatings) to enhance surface energy and promote subsequent adhesion. In a preferred embodiment, the surface preparation station comprises a series of spray or immersion cleaning tanks followed by hot air knife drying units to ensure the metal surface is substantially free of moisture and residual contaminants prior to entering the coating station.

### Adhesion Promoter Application Station

A distinguishing feature of the present invention resides in the adhesion promoter coating step, wherein a layer of adhesion-promoting composition is applied to at least one surface of each metal strip prior to lamination with the plastic core layer. The adhesion promoter composition may comprise one or more of the following: a chromate-free or chromate-containing primer, a silane-based coupling agent, an epoxy-based primer, a polyurethane-based primer, an acrylic-modified adhesion promoter, or a titanate or zirconate coupling agent, applied either as a solvent-based, water-based, or 100% solids formulation.

The adhesion promoter is applied by means of a roll coater, gravure coater, curtain coater, or spray coating apparatus disposed downstream of the surface preparation station. The coating apparatus is configured to apply the adhesion promoter at a controlled wet film thickness, typically ranging from about 0.5 microns to about 10 microns, corresponding to a dry film thickness of approximately 0.1 to 3 microns following solvent or carrier evaporation. Precision metering rolls or doctor blades may be employed to ensure uniform coating weight across the width of the metal strip, with coating weight typically maintained within a tolerance of ±10% across the strip width.

Following application, the coated metal strips are conveyed through a drying and/or curing oven maintained at a temperature and residence time sufficient to at least partially cross-link or cure the adhesion promoter composition, typically ranging from about 80°C to about 200°C for a dwell time of approximately 5 to 60 seconds, depending upon the specific chemistry of the adhesion promoter employed. In certain embodiments, the adhesion promoter is only partially cured at this stage, such that residual reactive functionality remains available to react with the thermoplastic core material during the subsequent lamination step, thereby forming covalent or strong physicochemical bonds at the metal-plastic interface.

### Thermoplastic Core Layer Feeding

Concurrently with the metal strip preparation, a thermoplastic core layer is supplied to the lamination zone. In one embodiment, the core layer is fed as a pre-formed continuous sheet unwound from a supply roll. In an alternative embodiment, the core layer is formed in-line by means of a slot-die extruder disposed directly upstream of the lamination nip, wherein molten thermoplastic resin—which may comprise polyethylene, polypropylene, polyvinyl chloride, polyethylene terephthalate, or blends and copolymers thereof, optionally containing fillers, flame retardants, or colorants—is extruded at a controlled thickness ranging from approximately 0.2 mm to about 5 mm, and at a melt temperature sufficient to promote intimate contact and interfacial bonding with the adhesion-promoter-coated metal strips.

### Lamination Station

The coated first metal strip, the thermoplastic core layer, and the coated second metal strip are subsequently brought into converging contact at a lamination nip defined by a pair of counter-rotating laminating rolls, at least one of which is heated to a surface temperature sufficient to soften or partially melt the surface of the thermoplastic core layer and/or activate the adhesion promoter coating, typically ranging from about 100°C to about 250°C. The laminating rolls apply a nip pressure ranging from approximately 0.5 to 10 MPa, sufficient to achieve intimate interfacial contact between the metal strips and the core layer while avoiding excessive deformation of the metal substrates.

In an alternative embodiment, the lamination station comprises a heated double-belt press configured to apply heat and pressure over an extended dwell zone, thereby providing increased residence time for interfacial bonding reactions to proceed to completion, particularly advantageous when processing thicker core layers or higher-viscosity thermoplastic materials.

### Cooling Station

Following lamination, the composite laminate is conveyed through a cooling station comprising a series of chilled rollers, water-cooled platens, or forced-air cooling zones configured to reduce the temperature of the laminate to below the softening point of the thermoplastic core, typically to a temperature below about 40°C, prior to subsequent handling operations. Controlled cooling rate is maintained to minimize residual stress and warpage in the finished laminate.

### Finishing Operations

The cooled composite laminate is thereafter subjected to one or more finishing operations, including edge trimming, protective film application, thickness gauging via non-contact sensors, surface inspection utilizing optical or ultrasonic scanning systems, and coiling or cutting to length in accordance with end-use specifications.

## PROCESS PARAMETERS AND VARIATIONS

In certain embodiments, the adhesion promoter coating step is applied to both surfaces of each metal strip that will contact the thermoplastic core layer, while the opposite (exterior) surface of each metal strip may receive a separate decorative or protective coating in a parallel or subsequent processing line. In other embodiments, the process further comprises an in-line quality control station employing peel-strength testing, infrared spectroscopic monitoring of adhesion promoter cure state, or thickness measurement to enable real-time feedback control of process parameters including line speed, coating weight, and lamination temperature.

It will be understood by those skilled in the art that the specific materials, temperatures, pressures, and dwell times disclosed herein are illustrative of preferred embodiments and may be varied according to the specific metal substrates, thermoplastic resins, and adhesion promoter chemistries selected, without departing from the scope and spirit of the present invention.

## CLAIMS (ILLUSTRATIVE)

1. A continuous process for bonding two metal strips to a plastic core layer, comprising: unwinding a first metal strip and a second metal strip; treating at least one surface of each metal strip; applying an adhesion promoter coating to the treated surface of each metal strip; at least partially curing the adhesion promoter coating; positioning a thermoplastic core layer between the first and second metal strips; laminating the metal strips and the core layer under heat and pressure to form a composite laminate; and cooling the composite laminate.

2. The process of claim 1, wherein the adhesion promoter comprises a silane coupling agent, an epoxy-based primer, or a polyurethane-based primer.

3. The process of claim 1, wherein the thermoplastic core layer is formed in-line by extrusion directly into the lamination nip.

4. The process of claim 1, wherein the adhesion promoter coating is applied by a roll coater and dried in an in-line oven prior to lamination.

5. The process of claim 1, further comprising real-time monitoring of adhesion promoter cure state or bond strength during continuous operation.

## Two-Stage Process for Producing Adhesion-Promoted Metal-Plastic Laminates

### CLAIM 1 (Independent Method Claim)

A process for producing a metal-plastic composite laminate, comprising:

**(a)** a first stage comprising:
   (i) unwinding a metal strip from a coil supply in a continuous pretreatment line;
   (ii) cleaning a surface of the metal strip to remove contaminants therefrom;
   (iii) applying an adhesion promoter composition to at least one surface of the cleaned metal strip to form an adhesion-promoter-coated metal strip;
   (iv) curing or drying the adhesion promoter composition on the metal strip; and
   (v) rewinding the adhesion-promoter-coated metal strip into a coated coil for storage or transport; and

**(b)** a second stage, spatially and temporally separate from said first stage, comprising:
   (i) unwinding the adhesion-promoter-coated metal strip from the coated coil in a continuous lamination line;
   (ii) feeding the adhesion-promoter-coated metal strip together with a plastic core material into a laminating station;
   (iii) heating at least one of the adhesion-promoter-coated metal strip and the plastic core material to a temperature sufficient to activate the adhesion promoter and/or soften the plastic core material;
   (iv) applying pressure to bond the adhesion-promoter-coated metal strip to the plastic core material to form a metal-plastic composite laminate; and
   (v) cooling and coiling or cutting the metal-plastic composite laminate.

### CLAIM 2 (Dependent — Pretreatment Line Details)

### CLAIM 9 (Independent — System Claim)

A manufacturing system for producing a metal-plastic composite laminate, comprising:

**(a)** a continuous pretreatment line comprising:

   a curing station downstream of the application station configured to cure the adhesion promoter composition; and
   a rewind station configured to coil the adhesion-promoter-coated metal strip; and

**(b)** a continuous lamination line, separate from the pretreatment line, comprising:

   a feed system configured to introduce a plastic core material together with the adhesion-promoter-coated metal strip;
   a heating station configured to heat at least one of the adhesion-promoter-coated metal strip and the plastic core material;
   a laminating station downstream of the heating station configured to apply pressure to bond the adhesion-promoter-coated metal strip to the plastic core material; and
   a cooling and take-up station configured to cool and coil or cut the resulting metal-plastic composite laminate.

A metal-plastic composite laminate produced by the process of claim 1.
